steward.role: Nation Steward of Republic of the Congo

hero.lead: A nation of 6.48 million with forest across nearly two-thirds of its land, and 36,785 cubic metres of renewable fresh water for every citizen.

stats.label: Natural resource rents, share of GDP

capital.heading: 25 instruments. Four bond issues since November 2025, finance for the forest, and programmes for schools, power, farms and cities.

record.text: Total public debt, estimated as a share of GDP at end-2025
Eurobond, 9.5% amortizing notes due 2036, priced 20 May 2026, which retired the 2032 notes
Extended Credit Facility of 2022, concluded March 2025: about $430 million disbursed; a new arrangement requested in 2026
Sustainable Congo Basin Forest Economies Program, Phase 1: the Congo share of a $1.02 billion programme, approved March 2026
Emission Reductions Payment Agreement, Sangha and Likouala: for 8.4 million tonnes of emission reductions through 2025

register.name: Eurobond, 9.5% amortizing notes due 2036
register.detail: Priced 20 May 2026 · Closed 26 May 2026 · $564 million of the 2032 notes bought back by tender · The rest of the 2032 notes called, settlement expected 12 June 2026
register.note: Ten-year notes that retired the 2032 bond
register.text: Dollar notes due 2036 whose proceeds repurchased the 9.875% notes due 2032 and refinanced short-term treasury bonds on the CEMAC regional market maturing between June and September 2026. They lengthen the maturity of the State’s debt.

register.name: Eurobond, 9.5% amortizing notes due 2035
register.detail: Priced 11 February 2026 · Closed 17 February 2026 · Concurrent tender: $354 million of the 2032 notes accepted, settled 23 February 2026
register.note: Issued with a buyback of part of the 2032 notes
register.text: Dollar notes due 2035, issued alongside a cash tender for the 9.875% notes due 2032. The proceeds refinance short-term treasury bonds on the CEMAC regional market maturing in March and April 2026.

register.name: Eurobond, 9.875% amortizing notes due 2032
register.detail: Priced 4 November 2025, $670 million · Tap priced 16 December 2025, $260 million · $354 million bought back February 2026 and $564 million May 2026 · The rest called, settlement expected 12 June 2026
register.note: $670 million and a $260 million tap (the sum is arithmetic)
register.text: Dollar notes that refinanced short-term treasury bonds on the CEMAC regional market falling due between November 2025 and February 2026. Within seven months they were bought back and called with the proceeds of the 2035 and 2036 notes.

register.name: Poultry and Aquaculture Development Project
register.detail: Approved 7 August 2026 · IDA · Protected Agricultural Zones
register.note: Feed, fingerlings and day-old chicks for local producers
register.text: Strengthens poultry and fish farming to reduce the country’s dependence on food imports, with better access to feed, fingerlings and day-old chicks, training, and climate-resilient infrastructure in selected Protected Agricultural Zones. It serves the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: AGIR governance programme, first additional financing
register.detail: Approved 24 April 2026 · IBRD, EUR 26.20 million · New result area: debt management, cash management and state enterprise governance · Closing extended to 31 December 2028
register.note: Adds debt and cash management to the 2023 programme
register.text: An IBRD top-up to the Accelerating Governance Institutional Reforms for Sustainable Services programme of 2023. It adds a result area on debt management, cash management and the governance of state-owned enterprises.

register.name: Sustainable Congo Basin Forest Economies Program, Phase 1
register.detail: Approved 31 March 2026 · IDA credit of EUR 100.50 million for the Republic of the Congo · Part of a $1.02 billion programme with Cameroon and the Central African Republic
register.note: The Congo share of a three-country forest programme
register.text: An IDA operation to improve forest management and strengthen forest value chains in Central Africa, expected to generate 220,000 jobs across the three countries. It serves the livelihood standard in forest communities.

register.name: Strengthening Urban Resilience Project
register.detail: Approved 30 October 2025 · Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire
register.note: About 575,000 residents expected to benefit
register.text: Reduces climate risks and strengthens urban infrastructure in the two main cities, Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire. It serves the shelter standard for about 575,000 residents.

register.name: Third Fiscal Management and Inclusive Growth Development Policy Financing
register.detail: Approved 20 June 2025 · The final operation of a series of three, 2022 to 2025
register.note: Revenue, public finance, social protection and electricity reforms
register.text: Budget support for revenue from the oil and non-oil sectors and better public financial management, with reforms for competition, the business environment, human capital, social protection and electricity access.

register.name: Strengthening Electricity Services (PASEL)
register.detail: Approved 26 June 2024
register.note: Improved electricity access for some 1.75 million people
register.text: Strengthens electricity services so that some 1.75 million people gain improved access to electricity. It serves the energy standard.

register.name: Transforming the Education Sector for Better Outcomes and Results (TRESOR)
register.detail: Approved 26 June 2024 · Program-for-Results · $80 million IDA and $15 million from the Global Partnership for Education
register.note: Co-financed with the Global Partnership for Education
register.text: Finances education reform against agreed results in schools. It is aimed at the education standard, which sets Coverage for the Republic of the Congo.

register.name: Second Fiscal Management and Inclusive Growth Development Policy Financing
register.detail: Approved 15 December 2023 · The second of a series of three
register.note: Budget support for reforms
register.text: Supports reforms in governance, public finance and inclusive growth. It was followed by the third and final operation in June 2025.

register.name: Accelerating Governance Institutional Reforms for Sustainable Services (AGIR)
register.detail: Approved 31 March 2023 · Program-for-Results · $45 million IBRD loan and $25 million IDA credit
register.note: Paid on verified results
register.text: Strengthens the institutions that deliver public services, with funds released against agreed results. A $30 million additional financing followed in April 2026.

register.name: Climate-Resilient and Inclusive Livelihoods Project (ProClimat Congo)
register.detail: Approved 23 March 2023 · $70 million IBRD loan and $12 million PROGREEN grant · Additional IDA credit of EUR 47.2 million signed 8 December 2023 · Closing 31 May 2028
register.note: Plus additional financing of EUR 47.2 million, December 2023
register.text: Supports rural livelihoods that withstand a changing climate. It serves the food and livelihood standards for farming households.

register.name: Digital Transformation Acceleration Project (PATN)
register.detail: Approved 2 June 2022 · IDA
register.note: Connectivity and digital services
register.text: Extends broadband and digital public services. The EIB and the European Union co-finance its European component.

register.name: Extended Credit Facility
register.detail: Approved 21 January 2022 · Sixth and final review 12 March 2025 · 200 percent of quota
register.note: About $430 million disbursed in all; a new arrangement has been requested
register.text: A three-year IMF arrangement, concluded with its sixth and final review in March 2025, when cumulative disbursements reached SDR 324 million (about $430 million). An IMF mission from 24 September to 7 October 2026 discussed the Government’s request for a new Extended Credit Facility; no staff-level agreement had been reached.

register.name: Kobikisa Health System Strengthening Project
register.detail: Approved 2 June 2021 · IDA
register.note: Free care for diseases such as malaria, and for pregnant women and children
register.text: Strengthens the health system and pays for free care for certain diseases such as malaria, free vaccines, and free care for pregnant women and children. Health coverage stands at 45 on the WHO index.

register.name: Emission Reductions Payment Agreement, Sangha and Likouala
register.detail: Signed 3 May 2021 · Results-based carbon payments · No payment made by 29 November 2024
register.note: For 8.4 million tonnes of emission reductions through 2025
register.text: Pays for verified reductions in emissions from deforestation across more than 12 million hectares in the north of the country. A World Bank mission in November 2024 recorded no payment yet; it expected a first performance payment of $8.37 million, including a $1 million advance, once its conditions were met.

register.name: PREFOREST Congo (FP159)
register.detail: Approved 19 March 2021 · Grant · Accredited entity: FAO · Total project value $46.6 million
register.note: Forest emissions in five departments of the south
register.text: A Green Climate Fund grant to cut forest loss from slash-and-burn farming and fuelwood in southern Congo, by securing land access for small farmers, building fuelwood and agroforestry systems and improving market access for farmer groups. It serves the food and livelihood standards while keeping the forest standing.

register.name: Social Protection and Youth Productive Inclusion Project (Lisungi)
register.detail: Approved 24 June 2020, $50 million · Additional IDA credit of EUR 74.9 million ($83.0 million), 2022 · Closing 30 June 2027
register.note: Cash transfers for poor households, and jobs for young people
register.text: Began as the Lisungi emergency response to COVID-19, with cash transfers to nearly 200,000 poor and vulnerable households. The additional financing extends the Lisungi safety net and adds productive inclusion for young people, which serves the livelihood standard.

register.name: Letter of Intent with the Central African Forest Initiative (CAFI)
register.detail: Signed in Paris 3 September 2019 · Allocation of up to $65 million for 2019 to 2025: $45 million from the CAFI Trust Fund and $20 million bilateral
register.note: Close to $120 million mobilised with co-financing (2025 annual review)
register.text: A partnership with the Central African Forest Initiative for the forests of the Republic of the Congo, with an initial allocation of up to $65 million for 2019 to 2025. CAFI’s 2025 annual review reports close to $120 million mobilised through its funding and partners’ co-financing.

register.name: Economic Diversification Support Program, Phase 1
register.detail: Approved 17 November 2023 · Loan · Budget support
register.note: To reduce dependence on oil
register.text: An African Development Bank loan for public investment management, the governance of public corporations, a new public procurement code, the business environment, electricity sector reform and productive sectors.

register.name: Digital transformation, European component (EIB loan)
register.detail: Signed 30 December 2022 · Co-finances the World Bank digital acceleration project · Launched 17 June 2025
register.note: European loan alongside a FCFA 10 billion EU grant
register.text: A European Investment Bank loan for governance through digitalisation, digital skills for employment, personal data protection, cybersecurity and priority IT systems in higher education and health.

register.name: Digital transformation, European component (EU grant)
register.detail: Signed 30 December 2023 · Grant · Launched 17 June 2025
register.note: EU grant alongside the EIB loan
register.text: A European Union grant to the same European component of the digital programme: governance through digitalisation, digital skills, data protection and cybersecurity.

register.name: Ecobank Congo, trade finance guarantee
register.detail: Announced 16 February 2026 · Covers up to 100% of the non-payment risk of banks confirming Ecobank Congo’s letters of credit
register.note: Trade, including essential foodstuffs such as oil and sugar
register.text: An African Development Bank guarantee that lets international banks confirm letters of credit issued by Ecobank Congo. It supports trade in health, education, transport and essential foodstuffs, which serves the food and livelihood standards.

register.name: BOA Congo, senior loan
register.detail: Announced 11 November 2025 · In CFA francs, about $25.5 million · Backed by the IDA Private Sector Window local currency facility · At least 10% for women-owned or women-led firms
register.note: More than 3,000 small businesses over five years
register.text: An IFC local-currency loan to Bank of Africa Congo for lending to micro, small and medium enterprises, expected to support 800 to 1,300 new jobs. It serves the livelihood standard.

assets.heading: Five assets no balance sheet counts.

items.name: The Forest
items.label: Of land under forest, 2024
items.text: Part of the Congo Basin, the second-largest tropical forest on Earth.
items.alt: The Congo Basin forest in the north of the Republic of the Congo

items.name: The Carbon
items.label: Up to, for 8.4 Mt of emission reductions
items.text: A results-based agreement covering more than 12 million hectares of Sangha and Likouala.

items.name: The Water
items.label: Renewable fresh water per person, 2022
items.text: Among the largest endowments of fresh water per citizen anywhere.

items.name: The Oil
items.label: Natural resource rents, share of GDP, 2021
items.text: The revenue that writes the budget.
items.alt: An offshore oil platform off Pointe-Noire

items.name: The People
items.label: Citizens, 2025
items.text: Nearly two in three live in cities, most of them in Brazzaville and Pointe-Noire.

enterprises.heading: Already working in Republic of the Congo.

items.name: SARIS Congo
items.text: The sugar production division of Somdia at Nkayi, which exported 3,066 tonnes of sugar to Gabon in 2023. Its molasses supply the country’s first ethanol distillery, a €23 million investment of over 6 million litres a year, opened in 2025.

items.name: La Congolaise des Eaux (LCDE)
items.text: A water utility. On 16 December 2025 it brought the Nkombo drinking water station into service, to supply more than 5,000 households in the 9th arrondissement of Brazzaville.

items.name: Centrale Électrique du Congo (CEC)
items.text: The power station at Pointe-Noire. In 2025 it generated 2.4 TWh, equivalent to approximately 50% of the electricity produced in the country.

items.name: BOA Congo
items.text: Bank of Africa Congo is lending an IFC loan of FCFA 14.5 billion (about $25.5 million) to micro, small and medium enterprises, with more than 3,000 small businesses expected over five years.
